title: Trademark vs. Copyright: Which One Is Right for You?
summary: While copyrights and trademarks both provide legal protection, they have distinct purposes. Learn more about the differences between the two.
body_text: What to do about infringement Now, let's consider infringements. Let's say there's a playground in your community with statues of popular Disney characters. The sculptures are obvious representations of characters from Disney movies. They are also obviously done by a local artist without official permission to use the likenesses from Disney. In this case, has an infringement taken place? To infringe a trademark or copyright, the infringer must trespass on what the intellectual property protects. The infringer must take a particular expression (like Snow White as a character from a film) or co-opt the goodwill built up by the company (Snow White as part of the Disney princess brand). For the fiberglass statue in the park, the infringement is a bit of both. The playground is taking the decisions that Disney made when designing the characters. Even if the execution is less than perfect, reproducing Disney's character's look uses a critical part of the animated film without permission. Moreover, the way the playground uses the characters is closely aligned with how Disney uses its princesses. The key legal question is whether the circumstances create confusion among consumers. This could involve a jury having to determine if the playground's use of Snow White might cause users to think that the playground is in some way associated with Disney. The fiberglass princesses may be a long way from Disneyland, but it may be reasonable to think that the maker of the statue or the park owner would have licensed rights from Disney to use its characters and trademarks. How to address infringement As you can imagine, determining copyright or trademark infringement can be a complicated and somewhat convoluted process. That said, if you believe someone has infringed upon your exclusive rights, we encourage you to consult an attorney specializing in trademark and copyright law. They can help determine if someone violated your rights and what next steps to take. This might involve sending a cease-and-desist letter and taking legal action. FAQs Is it better to have a copyright or trademark? One is not better than the other, as each has its own distinct purpose. In short, copyrights are for creative works, while trademarks are for names, slogans, and symbols associated with a brand. Therefore, in some cases, you may need both to protect your business’ branding and its creations. For example, if you run an art business, you might trademark your brand logo and company name and copyright your original artwork. How much does a copyright cost? When applying for a copyright, you must pay the associated filing fees, which depend on the works you register and how you file. An electronic single application for one work with one author costs $45 , while an electronic standard application for all other filings (such as multiple works by multiple authors) is $65. If you choose to mail in your application, the fee is $125. How much does a trademark cost? The cost of registering a trademark depends on which application you select and how many classes you register. The USPTO charges a base application fee of $350 per class of goods or services for all applications filed through the Trademark Center. The USPTO provides a list of trademark fees . If you hire a service like LegalZoom to run a comprehensive trademark search, packages start at $199. Can trademarks and copyrights be rejected? Yes, trademarks and copyrights can be rejected if they don't meet the eligibility requirements. The respective offices will contact you for additional information or changes in these cases. If you comply with the requests, then your application should be back on a path towards approval. How long do trademarks and copyrights last? To keep your trademark valid, you must file the appropriate maintenance documents. You need to file a "Declaration of Use under Section 8" between the fifth and sixth year from your registration date, while a "Declaration of Use and Application for Renewal under Sections 8 and 9" is due between the ninth and tenth year (and again every 10 years). If you fail to submit these documents, your trademark will be considered “abandoned,” and you will lose your exclusive rights. As for copyrights, they remain active for the duration of the author's life plus an additional 70 years. After that, the works enter the public domain. Corie Lynn Rosen contributed to this article.

title: AI In Healthcare: Real‑World Benefits For Clinical Teams
summary: Learn how AI helps streamline routine work and surface critical insights faster so that clinical teams can stay focused on care and improve workflow efficiency.
body_text: SUMMARY Clinical teams are under constant pressure to keep up with documentation, staffing demands, and an expanding volume of clinical data, often at the expense of face time with patients. Artificial intelligence (AI) is starting to relieve that strain by streamlining routine work and surfacing critical insights faster, helping teams stay focused on care while improving efficiency across everyday workflows. ​The daily challenges and the AI solution ​Clinical teams spend much of their day navigating workflows tied to patient care, from documenting encounters and coordinating care to managing an ever-growing volume of clinical information. The weight of administrative work has contributed to widespread burnout across nursing, provider, and support staff roles. HealthStream, a leader in healthcare workforce solutions, recognizes that the clinical teams carrying this burden need practical support, not added complexity. This is where AI in healthcare has become increasingly valuable: not as a futuristic concept, but as a working tool that's already helping teams do more of what matters. ​Easing administrative burdens ​A significant portion of a clinician's day is spent not in direct patient care, but on the documentation and administrative work required to support it. Studies consistently show that clinicians spend upwards of one-third of their working hours on indirect patient care and administrative tasks — entering orders, completing forms, managing referrals, and coordinating logistics. AI doesn’t eliminate the need for human oversight, but it can handle high-volume, repetitive tasks with speed and consistency, freeing clinical staff to spend more time face-to-face with patients. ​ ​Automating documentation and data entry ​One of the most time-consuming daily tasks for clinical staff is documentation. AI tools can transcribe spoken notes directly into electronic health record (EHR) systems, turning in-person encounters or verbal dictation into structured chart entries. AI can also automatically pull relevant data from lab results, prior visit summaries, and referral notes to pre-populate EHR fields. The result is straightforward: clinical teams spend less time on charting tasks and more time focused on direct patient care. ​In one example, a 2025 study published in "JAMIA Open" followed 84 pediatric providers across a six-month AI scribe pilot and found that documentation time dropped by nearly 21% per appointment — adding up to roughly 1.5 hours returned to each provider every week. Beyond the time savings, the share of providers reporting burnout fell from 55% to 33%. A 2025 study found that an AI-scribe pilot program reduced documentation time for providers by nearly 21%. ​Smarter workforce management ​Staffing is one of the most complex and high-stakes challenges in any hospital. Too few staff on a given shift puts patients at risk; too many puts needless strain on the budget. AI-powered scheduling tools analyze historical patient volume, seasonal trends, staff availability, and skill mix to help managers build schedules that better align with anticipated demand while reducing unnecessary labor costs. ​HealthStream’s hStream platform gives users access to data-driven scheduling support that connects workforce capacity with patient demand — assigning the right personnel to shifts without relying on guesswork or last-minute adjustments. When an unexpected surge in admissions occurs, predictive tools can alert managers early enough to respond before staffing imbalances take hold. ​The results can be substantial: A 2025 study in “npj Health Systems” found that predictive analytics deployed at the emergency department at Hackensack University Medical Center in New Jersey cut labor costs by $162 per hour (about $1.4 million in annual savings for a single ED) while keeping wait times and patient throughput unchanged.​ Predictive analytics saved one ED about $1.4 million annually while maintaining wait times and patient throughput, according to a 2025 npj Health Systems study. ​Enhancing clinical decision making ​The goal with AI isn't to hand over decisions to an algorithm, but to give providers faster access to better information so they can make more confident calls. When used thoughtfully, AI in healthcare acts as an additional layer of analysis that works alongside clinical expertise. ​Speeding up diagnostics ​Medical imaging is one area where AI has demonstrated consistent, measurable value. AI systems trained on large datasets of radiology images can analyze X-rays, CT scans, and MRIs to flag potential anomalies such as early-stage tumors, fractures, or signs of stroke for radiologist review. This doesn't mean a radiologist is taken out of the loop; it means the radiologist's attention is directed more efficiently. For example, a 2025 study published in the “ Journal of the American College of Radiology” found that AI-assisted review of CT scans significantly reduced radiologist report turnaround times for pulmonary embolism cases, helping urgent studies reach clinical attention faster.​ ​The same principle applies to lab results. AI tools can compare a patient's current labs against reference ranges and the patient’s own historical values, highlighting patterns that might otherwise take longer to notice. For busy clinical teams managing high patient loads, that kind of rapid triage helps reduce the risk that important findings are overlooked. ​Using predictive analytics for patient care ​One of the most promising applications of AI in healthcare is the ability to identify patients who are at risk of deteriorating. Predictive analytics tools continuously review patient data — vital signs, lab trends, medication records and clinical history — and generate risk scores that alert care teams when a patient's condition may be worsening. This kind of early warning capability is particularly valuable in high-acuity settings like the ICU or telemetry units, where rapid changes are common and early intervention is critical. ​A 2025 meta-analysis published in “ BMC Medical Informatics and Decision Making” found that AI-powered early warning systems can improve patient outcomes by helping clinicians identify signs of deterioration sooner and intervene before complications escalate. Emerging technologies such as digital twins may allow clinicians to model potential patient outcomes and evaluate treatment options using real-time patient data.​ ​From streamlined workflows to meaningful human connection ​As AI reduces time spent on documentation, record retrieval, and routine workflows, clinicians and teams gain faster access to the information they need and spend less time tied to a computer. That shift creates more space for direct interaction — listening, explaining, and building trust with patients during care encounters. AI can surface relevant data, flag potential risks, and handle repetitive tasks, but clinical judgment remains with the individuals delivering care, allowing those moments of face-to-face connection to take priority. ​ ​These benefits extend across the broader workforce as well. When administrative tasks are streamlined and information flows more efficiently, personnel can focus on coordination, communication, and support rather than navigation and rework. Reducing administrative strain not only helps address burnout but also creates a more sustainable environment where teams can stay engaged in the human side of care, even as demand and staffing pressures continue. ​Next steps for your clinical team ​The case for AI in healthcare is no longer theoretical. The core benefits, including reduced administrative burden, stronger clinical decision support and more time available for direct patient care, are already being realized by organizations across a wide range of care settings. ​When implemented thoughtfully, AI doesn't replace the expertise of clinicians and care teams, it helps them work more effectively. By reducing routine administrative work and improving access to timely information, AI can help organizations strengthen operations, support their workforce and deliver better care for patients.​ ​FAQs ​What are the benefits of AI in healthcare? ​AI helps clinicians spend less time on administrative work and more time on patient care. It can streamline documentation, support clinical decisions, improve staffing efficiency, and help identify at-risk patients earlier. Used responsibly, AI supports clinical teams while improving operational efficiency and care delivery. ​Can AI help reduce clinician burnout? ​Yes. By reducing documentation time and other repetitive administrative tasks, AI can help clinicians spend more time on patient care and less time on paperwork. This shift may improve job satisfaction and support a more sustainable work environment. ​ Can AI improve clinical decision making? ​AI helps clinicians access relevant information more quickly by analyzing large volumes of patient data, identifying patterns, and highlighting potential risks. Providers remain responsible for all care decisions, using AI as a support tool rather than a replacement for clinical judgment. ​What is predictive analytics in healthcare? ​Predictive analytics uses AI to analyze clinical data and identify patients who may be at higher risk for complications or deterioration. These insights help care teams intervene earlier and make more informed treatment decisions. ​Will AI replace healthcare professionals? ​No. AI is designed to support healthcare professionals, not replace them. While it can automate routine tasks and provide clinical insights, decisions about diagnosis, treatment, and patient care remain with qualified clinicians.

Most teams finish core setup in about three weeks. Data import and mapping usually eat around three days of that. On a 1-to-5 difficulty scale, Blixo lands at a 2. Competing AR suites tend to sit at 3 or 4. End-to-end automation shortens the invoice-to-cash cycle and cuts manual errors, which smooths cash flow for construction firms. Firms still tracking AR by hand tend to carry longer Days Sales Outstanding and more frequent cash gaps. Key takeaways Every tool here reduces manual invoicing. The difference is that Blixo folds collections, dunning, and cash application into one platform instead of leaving cash app for a separate system. Keeping those steps together means back-office teams communicate with clients on a consistent cadence, which cuts payment delays and administrative friction. How long does implementation take, and how hard is it? It depends on the size of your data set and how tangled your current workflows are. Blixo ships onboarding guides, data-import tools, and a configurable workflow engine to speed things along. Most customers wrap core setup in a few weeks, with extra time for training and fine-tuning. A typical rollout starts with data mapping to align customer accounts and active contracts, then moves to workflow configuration and team onboarding. What benchmarks should you watch? The moment you move from manual tracking to an automated system, you get real visibility into outstanding balances. That’s what lets accounting spot payment bottlenecks early and build cash-flow forecasts you can actually trust. When you plan a rollout, aim for: A measurable DSO drop within the first few months. Better cash-flow projection accuracy from automated payment matching and real-time reporting. Higher collection rates from automated reminders and dunning sequences. Hit those and you shorten the payment cycle, cut overhead, and keep projects moving without payment-related stalls. Why Manual AR Quietly Kills Construction Cash Flow Tie payment confirmation to automated reminders and collection actions, and you remove the manual bottlenecks that stall releases. The system watches invoice status, flags overdue items, and fires off follow-ups on its own. Money moves through the pipeline faster, without ad-hoc email chains or someone rekeying data at month-end. Which teams feel it first? Owners, accountants, and project managers all notice the difference early. Owners get a transparent process that heads off disputes. Accountants get one dashboard tracking invoices, payments, and collection activity. Project managers get real-time alerts when a payment is pending, so they can act before it turns into a roadblock. And everyone spends less time on manual reconciliation. Faster collections plus a unified view of receivables means contractors can fund the next phase without reaching for short-term financing. That last part matters. Bridging cash tied up in unpaid retainage is one of the most expensive workarounds in the business. When can you skip full automation? If you run a handful of active contracts and everyone’s already fully paper-free, the ROI on a comprehensive automated workflow is thin. A lightweight invoicing tool with e-signatures might carry you. But once contract volume climbs or payment cycles stretch out, the hidden cost of manual tracking usually outruns the effort of automating. Line up progress billing, real-time cash-flow projections, and automated collection actions, and you’ve got a single compliant engine that turns delayed payments into revenue you can forecast. Healthier balance sheet, fewer administrative headaches, and more attention for new work instead of chasing old invoices. Automating AR Workflows in Construction Blixo automates AR for construction firms by capturing electronic payments and applying cash-application rules in one platform. When a payment comes in, the system matches it to open invoices and updates the project’s financial record. Less manual effort, tighter grip on cash flow. What do electronic payments actually change? Payment portals give you real-time visibility into every incoming check or ACH transfer. Blixo’s matching engine reconciles payments to invoices quickly, which shortens the gap between invoicing and cash in the bank. How does automation handle construction billing? When a payment posts, Blixo updates the invoice status and reflects any retainage amounts you’ve configured. Project records stay accurate and stakeholders see current payment info without anyone touching a spreadsheet. Keeping your ERP in sync Blixo connects with QuickBooks, Xero, Sage Intacct, NetSuite, and custom ERP setups. A few practices worth following: Audit your current payment channels – figure out which clients pay by ACH, card portal, or mailed check. Configure automatic payment capture – set rules so bank-statement data flows straight into Blixo. Define invoice and retainage templates – bake in contract-specific percentages and approval authorities. Pilot on a low-risk project – confirm that payment → invoice update → ERP sync runs without manual intervention. Scale gradually – expand to bigger jobs once the pilot proves cash-application accuracy holds. Customers report significant drops in manual invoice-processing time after linking their payment channels to Blixo. Done in this order, existing accounting records stay clean through the migration. Fold automated cash application and payment tracking into the wider AR workflow, and a traditionally reactive process starts working ahead of you. Fewer delayed payments, lower processing costs, and a clean audit trail that keeps owners, lenders, and subs confident in every transaction. Streamlining Collections and Dunning for Construction Blixo’s AR automation simplifies collections and dunning across a construction project, from invoicing through payment confirmation. Automated reminders and customizable dunning workflows keep things moving while covering your projects’ documentation needs. Configuring collection rules The rule-builder lets you set thresholds that match your contract terms and trigger the right outreach automatically. Those rules stay fully editable, so you can tighten or loosen them as your cash-flow forecast shifts. And because the logic lives in the AR system, you drop the manual spreadsheets and every project follows the same cadence. Why automated dunning letters beat email chains Automated dunning letters replace the ad-hoc email threads that stall collections. Each letter pulls the latest invoice data, includes a direct payment link, and logs the outreach in the client’s activity feed. Many contractors see faster payment cycles once reminders run automatically. A dunning template that works usually has: A clear statement of the outstanding amount and original due date. A concise call-to-action with a one-click payment portal. A short note on any retainage that gets held if payment doesn’t land within the next 10 days. Every interaction is recorded, so you keep a traceable audit trail. Handling payment confirmation When a payment posts, Blixo updates the invoice status and can auto-send a receipt through the customer portal. That immediate confirmation keeps owners and general contractors in the loop and supports clean progression through project milestones. Best practices for transparent collections Publish a payment schedule on the client portal so stakeholders can see upcoming due dates and retainage triggers. Keep one source of truth – correspondence, dunning actions, and payment status all in the AR dashboard, so project managers can answer client questions on the spot. Review dunning outcomes weekly – use the built-in analytics to catch patterns, like a subcontractor who’s chronically late, and adjust contract terms before the next project. Configurable alerts, automated dunning, and real-time payment confirmations turn collections into a proactive cash-flow engine instead of a reactive chase. Construction firms keep projects on schedule without adding headcount. Building a Business Case for AR Automation in Construction The case for AR automation in construction rests on three measurable pillars: faster cash flow, lower compliance risk, and operational cost savings. Embed automated lien-waiver issuance directly into the AR workflow and you kill the manual hand-off that stalls payments and opens you to lien disputes. How to calculate ROI Factor in the technology investment: software licenses, integration effort, and training. The formula we use: ROI = (Annual cash‑flow gain + Compliance cost avoidance) ÷ Total implementation cost × 100%. What a practical rollout looks like Four short phases: assessment, configuration, pilot, and full-scale launch. 1. Assessment – Map every invoicing and lien-waiver touchpoint across active projects. Find the bottlenecks where manual paperwork causes delays. Those are your first automation targets. 2. Configuration – Set up rule-based triggers so that when an invoice posts, the system generates the matching lien-waiver and attaches it to the payment record. Use pre-built AIA-format templates to stay compliant without custom coding. 3. Pilot – Run the workflow on a single project team. Track time to generate a waiver, DSO, and error rate. Two weeks is usually enough to surface the integration quirks. 4. Full-scale launch – Roll out to all crews, refine rules based on pilot data, and set a governance cadence for ongoing improvement. Because the engine can auto-generate 10,000 invoices in 0.014 seconds, the technical setup rarely becomes the bottleneck. The real work is change management. Driving adoption without a fight You win user buy-in by tying the new workflow to performance incentives and giving people hands-on training that mirrors their actual day. Start with champion users, the project managers already comfortable with digital tools. Give them early access and ask them to document time saved. Their testimonials become your peer-to-peer proof. Then run short, role-specific workshops showing exactly how a payment receipt auto-creates a lien-waiver, killing the “where’s the right form” hunt everyone dreads. Finally, put up real-time dashboards showing each team’s DSO and waiver compliance rate. When the numbers improve, say so publicly. “Automating your entire accounts receivable process optimizes every step which results in improved cash flow by bringing money into your organization faster.” – a senior product marketing manager at a leading AR provider Pair those tactics with a clear ROI narrative and the business case becomes a story finance leaders can take to the board. For more on structuring cash-flow forecasts, see this construction consulting blog . Choosing the Right AR Automation Tool for Construction Picking a platform comes down to how well it handles the specialized parts of construction billing. The right tool connects billing events to compliance documentation cleanly, so payment milestones trigger the necessary releases without anyone stepping in. Start with a short feature checklist. The platform should handle progress billing and AIA-style invoices, apply retainage rules automatically, and trigger lien-waiver creation the instant retainage releases. Look for real-time cash-flow dashboards, integrated payment tracking, and a rule engine that maps contract milestones to billing events. Without those, you’re still juggling spreadsheets and paperwork. What capabilities to prioritize Focus on lien-waiver automation, retainage handling, progress-billing support, and clean ERP integration. You want a system that logs compliance events for audit automatically and applies contract-specific retainage rules without manual math. Built-in compliance checks that flag state-specific requirements before documentation is finalized are worth extra points. Lien rules vary by state, and that’s exactly the kind of detail that bites you later. How to judge scalability and integration fit Assess whether the tool can grow with your portfolio and speak the same language as your existing stack. A cloud-native platform that scales from a single-job pilot to dozens of concurrent sites saves you from a costly re-implementation down the road. Verify native connectors to the ERP systems you already run, whether Sage, NetSuite, or a custom job-costing setup, so invoice data, payment status, and lien-waiver records stay synced. Vendors reporting sub-ten-second processing per invoice typically enable a 30% DSO reduction in the first six months. When per-transaction costs drop to low single digits, the ROI shows up fast, often ahead of what a full-time controller would cost. What makes implementation go smoothly Start small, configure the lien-waiver trigger early, and invest in real training and support. Pilot on a single project that includes retainage and lien-waiver requirements. Configure the rule engine to issue a waiver when the retainage-release payment posts, then run a parallel manual check for the first two cycles. Use the vendor’s onboarding team to map your contract milestones to the system’s billing templates. That’s what prevents rework later. Train accounting staff and field supervisors together, because siloed training tends to leave field teams unaware the automated waiver workflow even exists. Then watch DSO, waiver-generation latency, and manual-entry hours to confirm the automation is delivering the cash-flow lift you expected. If you’re running fewer than five active jobs, the out-of-the-box rule set is plenty. Enterprise-grade customization rarely pays off for small crews. Frequently Asked Questions 1. Can I still gain benefits from Blixo if my existing ERP already handles invoicing? Yes. While ERPs excel at static record-keeping, they often lack dynamic communication features. Blixo sits on top of your ERP to manage customer outreach, automated reminders, and payment matching. Real-time native connectors ensure that as soon as a payment is reconciled, the updated status is reflected back in your ERP without manual data entry. 2. How does Blixo’s automated dunning handle partial payments or retainage releases? Partial payments and retainage releases trigger separate rule branches in Blixo. When a client pays only a portion of an invoice, the system records the amount, marks the remainder as outstanding, and continues the dunning schedule. Retainage rules automatically hold the specified percentage until the release event, then apply it to the open balance. 3. Is Blixo suitable for a contractor with only a few active jobs, or does it require enterprise‑level licensing? Small contractors can start with Blixo’s core module, which includes billing, collections, and cash‑application without requiring enterprise‑level licensing. The platform is designed to scale flexibly, offering tiered pricing structures that allow growing firms to pay only for the active volume they manage, avoiding unnecessary enterprise overhead. 4. What security and compliance measures does Blixo provide for electronic payment data? Blixo complies with SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 standards, encrypting all payment data at rest and in transit. Access is controlled through role‑based permissions and multi‑factor authentication, while audit logs capture every change. These safeguards meet most construction firms’ security policies and satisfy most client‑portal compliance requirements. 5. How does a modest DSO improvement—say five days—affect the ROI calculation for AR automation? If a firm improves DSO by only five days, the ROI formula still shows a positive return because each saved day translates into earlier cash for ongoing projects. Assuming an average invoice size of $150,000, five extra days free up roughly $75,000 in working capital, offsetting implementation costs within a year. 6. What are common pitfalls when migrating legacy invoice data into an automated AR system like Blixo? Common migration pitfalls include mismatched field formats, missing retainage percentages, and duplicate customer records. To avoid them, run a data‑validation script before import, map each legacy column to the corresponding Blixo field, and perform a pilot load on a low‑risk project. This reveals errors early and prevents downstream reconciliation issues.

title: Aramco Awards Halliburton Long-Term Contract for Unconventional Gas Program
summary: The Investor Relations website contains information about Halliburton's business for stockholders, potential investors, and financial analysts.
body_text: HOUSTON--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Jul. 15, 2026-- Aramco awarded Halliburton (NYSE: HAL) a multi-year contract to deliver integrated stimulation and completion services for unconventional gas development in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia. This award is part of a broader multi-billion contract, supporting one of the largest unconventional gas development programs globally. This award builds on Halliburton’s established portfolio supporting Aramco’s unconventional program. Across many of the Kingdom’s unconventional plays, Halliburton delivers a comprehensive suite of drilling and completion solutions. Its integrated service model is designed to support high-intensity development programs and improve operational efficiency, workflow predictability, and execution reliability. This collaboration supports broader regional efforts toward integrated unconventional development programs. “This award highlights our long-standing collaboration with Aramco and builds on more than 80 years in the Kingdom, while advancing unconventional gas development in the Kingdom,” said Rami Yassine, president, Eastern Hemisphere, Halliburton. “Beginning in the third quarter of 2026, Halliburton will deploy the Kingdom’s first fully integrated intelligent fracturing platform through OCTIV® Auto Frac and Sensori™ fracturing monitoring services to contribute to asset value for one of the world’s largest unconventional fields." Under the program, Halliburton will deploy intelligent automation solutions for fracturing to optimize performance in real time and support disciplined implementation across multi-well campaigns. These technologies support digital integration across operations while advancing efficiency and operational reliability. Development activities in the Jafurah Basin are underway. To support this effort, Halliburton plans to increase its investment in local manufacturing, improve its supply chain, and expand workforce development programs within the Kingdom, aiming to scale operations and sustain high performance as unconventional activity accelerates. ABOUT HALLIBURTON Halliburton is one of the world’s leading providers of products and services to the energy industry. Founded in 1919, we create innovative technologies, products, and services that help our customers maximize their value throughout the life cycle of an asset and advance a sustainable energy future.
